To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exponents which relate weights of links and strengths of nodes to their degrees have a geometric origin and that they are related to the dimensionality in which traffic networks reside.

the exponents of the power laws that relate the strength of nodes or links to their degrees in large traffic networks are universal, have a geometric origin, and are related to the dimensionality in which these networks are embedded.

(i) the scaling relations between strength of nodes and their degree and between weight of links and degrees of connected nodes have a geometric origin, (ii) the exponents in these relations can be calculated from the dimensionality of the space in which the network is embedded and (iii) these exponents are robust to the change of the dimensionality of embedding from 2D to 3D.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the origin of scaling exponents observed in real large scale networks and it is based on the assumption that these exponents are determined by geometry of the space in which the networks are embedded.

the observed scaling exponents in large traffic networks are a consequence of the geometry of the embedding space and are not a consequence of the dynamics of the system.
